configuration: Final store.Open configuration; both benchmark connections report SQLite synchronous=2 (FULL) and fullfsync=1 (ON).
note: Synthetic temporary SQLite files. Query medians use seven timed runs after two warmups. Writer timings are one sample per variant on a shared development host without concurrent audit benchmark jobs.
methodology: Two fresh store.Open temporary databases, WAL/FULL and fullfsync ON, foreign keys, 64MiB cache and 256MiB mmap. Current migrations apply to both; only the two new sort indexes are dropped in the baseline.
ANALYZE before queries; two warmups then median of seven runs per query. Queries fully scan and decode returned rows. No HTTP or network latency.
350k rows seeded in one recursive CTE INSERT. Writer samples add 10k synthetic rows in one INSERT and update name and consent for 10k rows in one UPDATE. Raw SQLite writes, not end-to-end CSV import.
File sizes measured after ANALYZE and WAL checkpoint, before 10k writer operations.
Host load, storage and fixture distribution affect latency. There is no p95 estimate; single writer samples are not stable write-penalty estimates.
observations: Name brand first/cursor medians fall from 67.7-111.7ms to 0.236-0.271ms in this final run.
Consent brand first/cursor medians fall from 99.8-122.3ms to 0.227-0.304ms with expression range seeking.
The new indexes add 14,213,120 bytes (18.38%) to this synthetic database.
Raw 10k INSERT is 171.604ms baseline versus 243.425ms indexed; raw 10k UPDATE is 23.156ms baseline versus 171.789ms indexed.
Selective prefix and list plans retain selective indexes. Custom sorts over these candidates can still use a temporary sort; every filter/sort combination was not indexed.
A large group equal to the consent cursor value may require checking IDs within that group. ID-only cursor anchors use the current row value, so deleted/edited anchors can end or move pagination.
